meanings.en: to be needed, to become necessary
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'надобиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'was needed', paired with 'требоваться'.

examples.text: Этот ключ мне больше не понадобится.
examples.trans: I won't need this key anymore.

examples.text: Если тебе понадобится помощь, скажи.
examples.trans: If you need help, tell me.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе, Марина. Этот ключ мне больше не понадобится.
examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. I won't need this key anymore.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'flounder' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Заходил, но я камбалу брал, а севрюгу нет.
examples.trans: I went in, but I took flounder, not stellate sturgeon.

examples.text: Затем в игру вступил Федя, которому понадобилась камбала.
examples.trans: Then Fedya entered the game, who needed flounder.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё пахнет, даже бумажка.
examples.trans: Everything smells nice, even the paper.

examples.text: Она мне даже не сказала, кто отец ребёнка.
examples.trans: She did not even tell me who the child's father is.

examples.text: Даже если и он, то что?
examples.trans: Even if it is him, then what?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Жених может поцеловать невесту.
examples.trans: The groom may kiss the bride.

examples.text: Я не опоздала?
examples.trans: Am I not late?

examples.text: Он не отец.
examples.trans: He is not the father.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'noticed', paired with 'замечать'.

examples.text: Федя даже не заметил, как рыба свалилась вниз.
examples.trans: Fedya did not even notice how the fish tumbled down.

examples.text: Он не заметил пропажу.
examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты её так смотришь, как будто жениться на ней будешь.
examples.trans: You are looking at it as if you are going to marry it.

examples.text: Пап, ты себя слышишь, какой зоопарк?
examples.trans: Dad, do you hear yourself, what zoo?

examples.text: Как можно было потащить ребёнка в подпольное казино?
examples.trans: How could you drag our child to an underground casino?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'валиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'fell / tumbled down'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и свалиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and fell on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют свалиться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to fell.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'downstairs', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Федя даже не заметил, как рыба свалилась вниз.
examples.trans: Fedya did not even notice how the fish tumbled down.

examples.text: Спускайтесь вниз.
examples.trans: Go downstairs.

examples.text: Он смотрит вниз.
examples.trans: He looks down.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Жених может поцеловать невесту.
examples.trans: The groom may kiss the bride.

examples.text: Все-таки ребёнку нужен отец.
examples.trans: After all, a child needs a father.

examples.text: Скажите ему, в законе такого нет.
examples.trans: Tell him there is no such thing in the law.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('empty').

examples.text: А потом пусть лечится.
examples.trans: And after that let him get treated.

examples.text: С полки в пустые коробки.
examples.trans: From the shelf into the empty boxes.

examples.text: Она вытащила пустые коробки из холодильника.
examples.trans: She pulled the empty boxes out of the cooler.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'boxes' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С полки в пустые коробки.
examples.trans: From the shelf into the empty boxes.

examples.text: Она вытащила пустые коробки из холодильника.
examples.trans: She pulled the empty boxes out of the cooler.

examples.text: Куда ты дела коробки из холодильника?
examples.trans: What did you do with the boxes from the cooler?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'any', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любой другой услышал бы звук падения, но не наш меломан.
examples.trans: Anyone else would have heard the sound of the fall, but not our music lover.

examples.text: В любой момент.
examples.trans: Any time.

examples.text: Любой человек это знает.
examples.trans: Anyone knows that.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('another').

examples.text: Из одного брака в другой без паузы.
examples.trans: From one marriage into another without a pause.

examples.text: Разводится со мной и выходит замуж за другого.
examples.trans: She is divorcing me and marrying someone else.

examples.text: Вика беременна, а он на другой женится?
examples.trans: Vika is pregnant, and he is marrying another woman?

meanings.en: to hear, catch the sound of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'слышать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'heard', paired with 'слышать'.

examples.text: Любой другой услышал бы звук падения, но не наш меломан.
examples.trans: Anyone else would have heard the sound of the fall, but not our music lover.

examples.text: Я рад это услышать.
examples.trans: I am glad to hear that.

examples.text: Они услышали громкий шум.
examples.trans: They heard a loud noise.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Рыба дорогая, должна быть в идеальном состоянии.
examples.trans: The fish is expensive, it must be in perfect condition.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, мне бы не хотелось, чтобы Элеонора Андреевна узнала.
examples.trans: Victor Petrovich, I would not want Eleonora Andreyevna to find out.

examples.text: Ну что, доча, обыграем дядю Мишу?
examples.trans: Well then, daughter, shall we beat Uncle Misha?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'sound' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Любой другой услышал бы звук падения, но не наш меломан.
examples.trans: Anyone else would have heard the sound of the fall, but not our music lover.

examples.text: Сделайте звук телевизора громче, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Turn up the volume on the television, please.

examples.text: Не дышать, я хочу слышать каждый тихий звук.
examples.trans: Do not breathe, I want to hear every quiet sound.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'fall' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Любой другой услышал бы звук падения, но не наш меломан.
examples.trans: Anyone else would have heard the sound of the fall, but not our music lover.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть падение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always fall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну, этот раз не в счёт, ладно?
examples.trans: Well, this time does not count, alright?

examples.text: Элеонора Андреевна, звали?
examples.trans: Eleonora Andreyevna, did you call for me?

examples.text: Я уговорила медийного человека сыграть у нас свадьбу.
examples.trans: I persuaded a famous person to hold a wedding here.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'music lover' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Любой другой услышал бы звук падения, но не наш меломан.
examples.trans: Anyone else would have heard the sound of the fall, but not our music lover.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть меломан.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always music lover.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Все-таки ребёнку нужен отец.
examples.trans: After all, a child needs a father.

examples.text: Скажите ему, в законе такого нет.
examples.trans: Tell him there is no such thing in the law.

examples.text: Я больше не буду так, клянусь.
examples.trans: I will not do that anymore, I swear.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё ясно, сделаем на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Everything is clear, we will do it at the highest level.

examples.text: Всё пахнет, даже бумажка.
examples.trans: Everything smells nice, even the paper.

examples.text: Молодец, Виктория всё продумала.
examples.trans: Well done, Victoria thought everything through.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Жених может поцеловать невесту.
examples.trans: The groom may kiss the bride.

examples.text: Все-таки ребёнку нужен отец.
examples.trans: After all, a child needs a father.

examples.text: Муж имеет право знать, кто отец ребёнка.
examples.trans: A husband has the right to know who the child's father is.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.text: Рыба дорогая, должна быть в идеальном состоянии.
examples.trans: The fish is expensive, it must be in perfect condition.

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.
examples.trans: Childhood was hard.
